intro.author: Not named. Jewish tradition in the Talmud credits Samuel. The closing family line ending with David shows it was completed after David became well known.
intro.written: Uncertain; proposals range from the time of David and Solomon (around 1000–900 BC) to after the exile
intro.audience: Israelites who knew David as their great king and wanted to know where his family came from
intro.setting: The story takes place 'in the days when the judges ruled' (1:1), the same troubled era as the book of Judges, but it moves at the quiet pace of one family. Famine drives a family from Bethlehem to Moab, east of the Dead Sea. In Hebrew Bibles Ruth stands among the Writings and is read at the Feast of Weeks, a harvest festival.
intro.purpose: To show God's hidden care at work through loyal, kind people, and to trace King David's line back to a Moabite woman who chose Israel's God.
intro.bigIdea: Through ordinary acts of loyal love, God turns emptiness into fullness and prepares the way for a king.
